info.title: EmmiTec Partner API
info.description:
Store readings from Bluetooth medical devices on the EmmiTec platform from your own app and backend, and receive alert payloads (title, text, reason and the reading that triggered them) to build your own push notifications.

Test and live use the same base URL. The key prefix decides the mode: `emk_test_` keys use an isolated sandbox where no clinician is ever notified; `emk_live_` keys use your real client and readings reach the care team. Every response has `X-Request-Id`; authenticated responses also have `X-EmmiTec-Mode`.

JSON only, UTF-8. Dates are ISO 8601 UTC with `Z`. Lists are newest first with `limit` (1 to 100, default 25) and an opaque `cursor`. Rate limit: 30 requests per second per key or session token.

servers.description: Production. Test and live share it; the key decides the mode.

tags.description: Store device readings and read them back with their level and alert.

tags.name: Alert settings
tags.description: Decide if your integration uses alerts, and set the limits that trigger them: per patient, or as the defaults of your live client. Patients can also have alerts turned off per type.

tags.name: Webhook
tags.description: One webhook per integration and mode. EmmiTec POSTs signed events to your HTTPS endpoint.

post.description:
**Token:** Secret key. A session token gets 403 `forbidden`.

Creates a token for ONE patient. Call it from your backend and hand the token to your mobile app (the @emmitec/rpm SDK uses it). A test key mints `emst_test_...`, a live key mints `emst_live_...`. The token is shown only in this response. Default lifetime 7 days (604800 s), min 300 s, max 30 days (2592000 s). Revoke with `DELETE /patients/{id}/session-tokens`. 

A session token can only call: `GET /ping`, `GET /me`, `GET /devices`, `POST /readings`, `POST /readings/batch`, `GET /readings/{id}`, and `GET /patients/{id}/readings` and `GET /patients/{id}/thresholds` for its own patient. Anything else gets 403 `forbidden`.

delete.description:
**Token:** Secret key. A session token gets 403 `forbidden`.

post.description:
**Token:** Secret key or session token. With a secret key, `patientId` is required. With a session token it may be omitted; if sent, it must be the patient of the token.

Stores one reading, evaluates it against the thresholds of the patient and returns it with `level`, `levels` and `alert` (null when the level is normal or unknown). `measuredAt` must not be more than 10 minutes in the future nor older than 365 days. Idempotent: the same `externalId` again (or, without `externalId`, the same patient + type + measuredAt + values) answers 200 with the original reading and `duplicate: true`. Values are returned in the canonical unit; weight readings get `bmi` when the patient has `heightCm`.

200.description: Duplicate: the reading was already stored. The original is returned with `duplicate: true`.

get.description:
**Token:** Secret key or session token. Session token: only for its own patient (`id` must be the patient of the token), else 403 `forbidden`.

The limits used to compute `level` and `alert`. `source` is `patient` when the patient has limits of their own (set by the care team or with `PUT /patients/{id}/thresholds`), `default` when they come from the client default. Missing limits are null; a value without limits gets level `unknown`.

put.summary: Set the limits of a patient
put.description:
**Token:** Secret key. A session token gets 403 `forbidden`.

Sets the limits of one patient for one type. They are the same limits the care team sees and edits in the EmmiTec portal, and the next readings of this patient use them right away. In `limits`, send the values you want to change, each with its four limits as numbers (0 to 1000) in order: criticalLow <= attentionLow <= attentionHigh <= criticalHigh. Values you do not send keep the limits that apply today; when one of them has no limits to keep, the API answers 400 with `param` `limits.<value>` (send that value too). Values per type: blood_pressure `systolic`, `diastolic` (mmHg), `pulse` (bpm); oxygen_saturation `spo2` (%), `pulse` (bpm); temperature `temperature` (C); glucose `glucose` (mg/dL). weight has no limits (400). The response lists every value of the type, all with `source: "patient"`.

oxygenSaturation.summary: Oxygen saturation: SpO2 (no high alert) and pulse

200.description: Every value of the type, with the limits that now apply.

bloodPressure.summary: Blood pressure (pulse was not sent and kept its limits)

put.summary: Turn alerts on or off for a patient
put.description:
**Token:** Secret key. A session token gets 403 `forbidden`.

Per patient and type. It is the same switch the care team has in the EmmiTec portal. Off: readings of this patient and type are still stored and get `level` and `levels`, but `alert` is null and no `reading.alert` event is sent. In test mode, `POST /sandbox/simulate-alert` turns alerts back on for the simulated type.

off.summary: No blood pressure alerts for this patient

get.summary: List the default limits of your client
get.description:
**Token:** Secret key. A session token gets 403 `forbidden`.

The default limits of the client of this mode: the shared sandbox defaults with a test key, the defaults of your live client with a live key. They apply to every patient that has no limits of their own (`GET /patients/{id}/thresholds` shows what applies to one patient). Values without default limits are left out.

put.summary: Change the default limits of your live client
put.description:
**Token:** Secret key, live mode only (`emk_live_...`). A test key or a session token gets 403 `forbidden`.

Live key only. A test key gets 403 `forbidden`: the sandbox defaults are shared by every partner, so set limits per patient with `PUT /patients/{id}/thresholds`. Send one type per call and, in `limits`, the values to change, each with its four limits (same rules as `PUT /patients/{id}/thresholds`). Values you do not send keep their defaults. The new defaults apply to every patient of your live client without limits of their own, including patients the care team added outside the API. 409 `conflict` when your client has no default limits for this type yet: EmmiTec sets them up.

200.description: The defaults of the type, as saved.

get.description:
**Token:** Secret key. A session token gets 403 `forbidden`.

Whether alerts are on for your integration in the mode of the key. Test and live have separate settings. Default: on.

put.description:
**Token:** Secret key. A session token gets 403 `forbidden`.

Turns alerts on or off for your integration in the mode of the key. Off: readings are still stored and still get `level` and `levels`, but `alert` is null in every response (and in the SDK), `reading.alert` is not sent, and `reading.created` (when subscribed) is still sent with `alert: null`. It only changes what EmmiTec sends to you: in live mode the readings still reach the care team.

**Token:** Any token (secret key or session token).

The v1 catalog, plus `manual` (typed by a person) and `other` (a device not in the catalog). Send the `model` in `device.model` of a reading. `pairing: true` means the device must be paired with the phone first (`uam820bt` asks for a pairing code). `hc059` sends its weight by Bluetooth advertising only (no connection).

post.description:
Sent when a reading has a level that is not normal or unknown. Default subscription. `data` has the patient, the reading (without `alert`) and the alert to turn into a push notification.

**Delivery.** EmmiTec POSTs the event to your URL with `Content-Type: application/json`. A 2xx answered within 10 seconds means delivered. Anything else is retried with backoff: 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h, 12 h (8 attempts total, about 22 h), then the event is marked `failed` (see `GET /events` and `POST /events/{id}/resend`). Delivery is at-least-once: dedupe by the event `id`. Order is not guaranteed: use `data.reading.measuredAt`.

**Verify every request.** Read `t` and `v1` from `EmmiTec-Signature`, compute HMAC-SHA256 with your webhook secret (`whsec_...`) over the string `<t>.<raw body>` (the RAW request body, before any JSON parsing), compare the hex result with `v1` in constant time, and reject the request when |now - t| is more than 300 seconds.

parameters.description: Event id, same as `id` in the body. Dedupe by it.

parameters.name: EmmiTec-Event-Type
parameters.description: Event type, same as `type` in the body.

parameters.name: EmmiTec-Signature
parameters.description: Format `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where v1 = hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>"). Reject the request when |now - t| > 300 s. The example was computed with the example secret `whsec_N4vX8qL2mR7tY1pK9sD3fG6hJ0wZ5cB8eQ2ua1b2` over the compact JSON of the example body.

bearerAuth.description:
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request. Two kinds of token:

- **Secret key** (`emk_test_...` or `emk_live_...`): generated in the customer portal (https://emmitec.health/portal), where you can copy it again at any time, or issued by EmmiTec. Only EmmiTec revokes keys. Server to server only: never ship it inside a mobile app or a website.
- **Patient session token** (`emst_test_...` or `emst_live_...`): minted by your backend with `POST /patients/{id}/session-tokens` for ONE patient and handed to your mobile app. It can only call `GET /ping`, `GET /me`, `GET /devices`, `POST /readings`, `POST /readings/batch`, `GET /readings/{id}`, and `GET /patients/{id}/readings` and `GET /patients/{id}/thresholds` for its own patient; anything else gets 403 `forbidden`.

Missing, invalid, revoked or expired token: 401 `unauthorized`.

XRequestId.description: Id of this request. Also in `error.requestId`. Send it to EmmiTec when you need help.

XEmmiTecMode.description: Mode of the key or token used: `test` or `live`. Present on every authenticated response.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor. Pass the `nextCursor` of the previous page.

From.name: from
From.description: Only readings measured at or after this instant (ISO 8601 UTC).

To.name: to
To.description: Only readings measured at or before this instant (ISO 8601 UTC).

Locale.name: locale
Locale.description: Language of the alert texts (`title`, `text`, `reason`): `en`, `pt` or `es`. Default: the webhook locale of your integration for this mode, else `en`.

AcceptLanguage.name: Accept-Language
AcceptLanguage.description: Alternative to the `locale` query parameter, same values (`en`, `pt`, `es`). Default: the webhook locale of your integration for this mode, else `en`.

code.description:
Exact cause:
- `invalid_json`: 400: the body is not valid JSON.
- `validation_failed`: 400: a field or parameter is invalid (see `param`).
- `unsupported_type`: 400: `type` is not one of the supported reading types.
- `unknown_device`: 400: `device.model` is not an id from `GET /devices`, `manual` or `other`.
- `unauthorized`: 401: token missing, invalid or revoked, or expired.
- `forbidden`: 403: session token outside its scope, live key when the integration has no live client, live key on a sandbox helper, test key on `PUT /thresholds`, or the integration is suspended.
- `not_found`: 404: not found for this integration and mode.
- `conflict`: 409: conflict, for example an email already used by another person on the client, or no default limits to change for this type.
- `patient_disabled`: 422: the patient is disabled for measurements.
- `rate_limited`: 429: more than 30 requests per second for this key or session token.
- `internal_error`: 500: unexpected error. The message is generic; the requestId is in our logs.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Never contains the token.

param.description: Field or parameter that caused the error, as a dot path (for example `values.systolic`). null when none.

requestId.description: Same value as the `X-Request-Id` response header. Send it to EmmiTec when you need help.

examples.message: values.systolic must be an integer between 40 and 300.

trialEndsAt.description: When the trial ends. null when the plan is not `trial`.

daysLeft.description: Whole days until `trialEndsAt` (rounded up, never negative). null when the plan is not `trial`.

module.description: Module of the integration. `rpm` (remote patient monitoring) is the only one in v1.

Ping.description: Result of `GET /ping`: who is calling, in which mode, and the plan of the integration.

ok.description: Always true when the token works.

integration.description: The integration that owns the token.

Alert.description: What you turn into a push notification. `title` is short, for the notification title. `text` is patient-facing, in plain language, about the patient ("your"). `reason` is technical, for logs and clinicians, and says which value crossed which limit. Texts never give medical advice; on critical levels `text` ends with "If you feel unwell, contact your care team or emergency services." Level words: en very high, high, low, very low; pt muito alta, alta, baixa, muito baixa; es muy alta, alta, baja, muy baja.

Limits.description: The four limits of one value, in the unit of the value (mmHg, bpm, %, C, mg/dL). All four are required, as numbers from 0 to 1000 (rounded to 2 decimals), and must satisfy criticalLow <= attentionLow <= attentionHigh <= criticalHigh. A reading at or above `criticalHigh` is critical_high, at or above `attentionHigh` attention_high, at or below `criticalLow` critical_low, at or below `attentionLow` attention_low, else normal.
